questions.question: Is 'given a DFA D, is L(D) empty?' decidable?
questions.solutionApproach: Yes — check if any accepting state is reachable from the start state via BFS/DFS on the DFA's transition graph. This is a simple, always-halting algorithm.
questions.answer: Decidable — reachability check on the DFA graph.

questions.question: Is 'given a Turing machine M, is L(M) empty?' decidable?
questions.solutionApproach: No — 'is L(M) empty' is a non-trivial semantic property of the TM's language. By Rice's Theorem, this is undecidable.
questions.answer: Undecidable — by Rice's Theorem (non-trivial semantic property of a TM's language).

questions.question: If both L and complement(L) are known to be Recursively Enumerable, what can you conclude about L?
questions.solutionApproach: By the theorem, L is Recursive (decidable) — this is exactly the iff condition.

questions.question: Sketch a reduction-based proof that 'given TM M, does M halt on ALL inputs?' is undecidable.
questions.solutionApproach: Assume decidable via decider D. Given an arbitrary (TM T, input w) instance of the Halting Problem, construct TM M' that: ignores its own input, simulates T on w, and halts if/when T halts on w (loops forever otherwise). M' halts on ALL inputs iff T halts on w. Run D on M' — this decides whether T halts on w, solving the Halting Problem. Contradiction, since Halting Problem is undecidable.
questions.answer: Reduction from Halting Problem via constructing M' that halts-on-all-inputs iff the original (T,w) halts — contradiction proves undecidability.
